s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent cough, hemoptysis, and chest pain with acute kidney injury and multifocal pneumonia
salient_findings: Acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine
Bilateral scattered infiltrates and peripheral patchy consolidations on chest imaging
key_facts: Elevated blood urea nitrogen (107 mg/dL) and creatinine (5.8 mg/dL)
Bilateral scattered infiltrates and denser consolidation on chest radiograph
Multiple peripheral patchy consolidations on noncontrast chest CT
Received intravenous azithromycin, ceftriaxone, and bicarbonate

shortlist.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pulmonary-renal syndrome with hemoptysis and acute kidney injury

shortlist.label: Goodpasture syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hemoptysis and acute kidney injury with anti-glomerular basement membrane disease

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent cough, hemoptysis, and chest pain with multifocal pneumonia

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Pulmonary-renal syndrome with acute kidney injury and leukocytosis

shortlist.label: Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hemoptysis and acute kidney injury with anti-glomerular basement membrane disease

raw.rationale: The combination of hemoptysis, renal failure, and pulmonary infiltrates is highly suggestive of Goodpasture syndrome, an autoimmune disease characterized by anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies.

rejected.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
rejected.why: While it can cause similar symptoms, the lack of specific granulomatous findings on imaging and the presence of anti-glomerular basement membrane disease-like symptoms make it less likely.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Similar to Wegener's, the clinical presentation does not strongly support granulomatosis with polyangiitis, especially without clear granulomatous inflammation on imaging.

rejected.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with renal involvement and pulmonary hemorrhage but is less commonly associated with the distinct anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies suggested by the clinical scenario.

rejected.label: Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease
rejected.why: This is essentially another term for Goodpasture syndrome, making it redundant to consider as a separate diagnosis given the champion choice.
